chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Hallal al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about two men who fought while they were both in Ihram. He said: 'Glory be to Allah, evil is what they have done.' I said: 'They have done it, so what is required of them?' He said: 'Upon each one of them is blood (damm).'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to Allah (expression of disapproval here)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَانِ: Two men in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation (damm) for two men fighting while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific legal consequence of physical combat between two pilgrims in Ihram, declaring the act reprehensible and mandating that each party individually pays 'damm' (blood sacrifice). This ruling highlights the principle that the violation of Ihram sanctity through mutual aggression incurs a personal penalty for each combatant, distinct from the general expiations for other Ihram breaches. The emphasis on individual liability underscores the seriousness of disrupting the spiritual state of pilgrimage through physical conflict.
